title: PARTNER CONTENT: Three Physical Walls Are Hitting AI Datacenter Infrastructure at the Same Time - And the Compound Effects Are Worse
gist: In vendor-supplied partner content, xFusion argues that AI datacenters face three physical walls at once (cooling, power delivery and electrical interconnect) as racks move from 240 kW in 2026 to megawatt-class, with chips above 3,000W. It pitches diamond-copper cold plates rated above 4,000W per chip, 800V HVDC distribution that it says cuts I²R losses about 220x compared with 54V, and 224G backplanes moving toward optics. Its central claim is that the three must be co-optimized, which it calls "computing-power synergy".

insights.claim: According to xFusion, AI accelerator rack power rose from about 20 kW in 2023 (350W chips) to 50 kW in 2024 (700W), 120 kW in 2025 (over 1,000W chips, 50-100 W/cm² heat flux) and 240 kW in 2026 (over 2,000W chips, 120 W/cm²).
insights.so_what: Rack power density is rising in steps, forcing infrastructure refreshes for cooling and power vendors.
insights.locator: Here is a trajectory that should focus
insights.speaker: xFusion

insights.claim: xFusion says the next generation of AI racks, already in validation at multiple hyperscalers, targets megawatt-class racks, chips above 3,000W and heat flux above 200 W/cm².
insights.so_what: Megawatt racks will require new power distribution and liquid cooling designs.
insights.locator: The next generation - already in validation
insights.speaker: xFusion

insights.claim: xFusion argues that cooling, power delivery and interconnect constraints compound: liquid cooling with legacy 54V power is throttled electrically, 800V power with weak optical fabric strands GPUs, and fast networking behind thermally throttled compute wastes capital, so all three must be co-optimized.
insights.so_what: Buyers should evaluate datacenter infrastructure as an integrated system rather than separate procurement categories.
insights.quote: solving any two while ignoring the third still results in stranded infrastructure
insights.locator: That is not a gentle curve.
insights.speaker: xFusion

themes.theme: Thermal wall and liquid cooling materials

insights.claim: xFusion states that air cooling is finished for high-density AI racks: at 200+ W/cm², convective air cannot remove heat fast enough to prevent throttling, leaving cold-plate direct liquid cooling as the only viable path.
insights.so_what: Direct liquid cooling becomes mandatory, supporting demand for DLC suppliers.
insights.quote: Air cooling is finished for high-density AI racks.
insights.speaker: xFusion

insights.claim: xFusion's diamond-copper composite cold plates have equivalent thermal conductivity above 650 W/m·K, about twice pure copper's, handling 200 W/cm² on average and over 400 W/cm² at hot spots, for total single-chip cooling capacity above 4,000W, about 33% headroom over coming 3,000W chips.
insights.so_what: Advanced thermal materials like diamond composites become a differentiator as chip power rises.
insights.locator: xFusion's approach is to use diamond-copper
insights.speaker: xFusion

insights.claim: xFusion is developing two-phase jet cooling, which uses liquid-to-gas phase change to cut coolant flow rates for the same thermal load, though sealing, pressure management and blind-mate connectors remain substantial challenges.
insights.so_what: Two-phase cooling is the next step if single-phase DLC runs out of headroom.
insights.speaker: xFusion

insights.claim: xFusion's FusionPod for AI V8, a 42U liquid-cooled rack rated up to 155 kW, uses a distributed CDU architecture that needs no secondary piping changes, which xFusion says cuts retrofit deployment from years to months.
insights.so_what: Retrofit-friendly liquid cooling can speed AI deployments in existing facilities.
insights.speaker: xFusion

insights.claim: At 54V distribution, a 1 MW rack draws 18,519 amps; since I²R losses scale with current squared, a 25x rise in rack power from 40 kW to 1 MW raises resistive losses 625x, so busbar losses can exceed 50 kW per rack and busbars can weigh over 200 kg.
insights.so_what: 48V-class distribution cannot scale to megawatt racks, forcing a voltage shift.
insights.speaker: xFusion

insights.claim: xFusion says moving from 54V to 800V DC cuts current about 15x and I²R losses about 220x, reduces conversion stages from four to three, raises end-to-end efficiency from about 88% to above 90%, and cuts line losses from 5-8% to under 1%.
insights.so_what: 800V HVDC is a big efficiency lever and an opportunity for power-electronics suppliers.
insights.locator: The solution is straightforward in principle
insights.speaker: xFusion

insights.claim: xFusion is building an 800V HVDC Sidecar power supply prototype for 300 kW to 1.2 MW per rack, with a roadmap toward direct 800V HVDC that removes more conversion stages and natively supports green power integration.
insights.so_what: Vendors are productizing megawatt-rack power delivery.
insights.speaker: xFusion

insights.claim: xFusion uses wide-bandgap devices across the power chain: SiC MOSFETs for AC-to-HVDC rectification, GaN HEMTs for HVDC-to-DC conversion at 800 kHz-1 MHz, and GaN multi-phase regulators for the 54V-to-12V/6V stage, where higher switching frequencies shrink magnetics and raise power density.
insights.so_what: The 800V transition drives SiC and GaN demand in datacenters.
insights.speaker: xFusion

insights.claim: xFusion is advancing vertical power delivery, placing conversion modules directly behind the chip package, which it says shortens the power path by about 90% and reduces resistive losses and transient-response problems.
insights.so_what: Vertical power delivery is an emerging design trend for kilowatt-class chips.
insights.locator: The company is also advancing vertical power
insights.speaker: xFusion

themes.theme: Interconnect wall and open Super Node

insights.claim: xFusion says 224 Gbps-per-lane copper signaling is already at the edge of signal integrity, and beyond 224G copper physics become unforgiving, making co-packaged optics necessary for large scale-up AI domains.
insights.so_what: Copper-to-optics transition in AI interconnect is underway.
insights.speaker: xFusion

insights.claim: xFusion has commercially deployed 224G orthogonal backplanes, is pre-researching 448G, and offers a Super Node open-architecture liquid-cooled system with up to 240 kW per rack and 128 XPUs per cabinet (256 across two), designed for multi-vendor processors as a hedge against accelerator market fragmentation.
insights.so_what: Multi-vendor open systems reduce lock-in to any one accelerator's proprietary interconnect.
insights.speaker: xFusion

insights.claim: xFusion's Arthur Wang frames AI datacenter value as a chain from WATT to FLOPS to TOKEN to AGENT to VALUE, arguing that competitiveness depends on business value extracted per watt rather than chip count.
insights.so_what: Energy efficiency per useful output, not raw chip count, as the key AI infrastructure metric.
insights.quote: competitiveness is not about how many chips you have. It is about how much real business value you can extract from every watt and every joule of heat.
insights.locator: As Wang put it at OCP
insights.speaker: xFusion
